pr_body:
`blob:` should be valid URL schemes.

A valid blob scheme can be represented as follows:  
   - new Uri("blob:http://host/absolute/")
   - new Uri("blob:https://mdn.mozillademos.org/ca45b575-6348-4d3e-908a-3dbf3d146ea7")

---

Multiple tests were added

Before modification the following error was thrown:  ` System.ArgumentException : Only 'http' and 'https' schemes are allowed. (Parameter 'requestUri')`  

```
test[0]
        [FAIL] System.Runtime.InteropServices.JavaScript.Http.Tests.HttpRequestMessageTest.Ctor_AbsoluteBlobStringUri_CorrectValues 
  dbug: test[0]
        System.ArgumentException : Only 'http' and 'https' schemes are allowed. (Parameter 'requestUri')      
  dbug: test[0]
           at System.Net.Http.HttpRequestMessage.InitializeValues(HttpMethod method, Uri requestUri)
  dbug: test[0]
           at System.Net.Http.HttpRequestMessage..ctor(HttpMethod method, String requestUri)
  dbug: test[0]
           at System.Runtime.InteropServices.JavaScript.Http.Tests.HttpRequestMessageTest.Ctor_AbsoluteBlobStringUri_CorrectValues()
  dbug: test[0]
           at System.Reflection.RuntimeMethodInfo.Invoke(Object obj, BindingFlags invokeAttr, Binder binder, Object[] parameters, CultureInfo culture)   
  dbug: test[0]
        Finished System.Private.Runtime.InteropServices.JavaScript.Tests, Version=5.0.0.0, Culture=neutral, PublicKeyToken=cc7b13ffcd2ddd51

```
---

Modify exception message to throw `Only 'http' 'https' and 'blob' schemes are allowed.` for browser.

---

Should be back ported to 5.0

issue_context.title: [wasm] HttpClient 5.0 no longer supports Blob URLs
issue_context.body:
### Describe the bug
I am testing updating some of my libraries to .net 5.0 and ran into issue where requesting blob urls no longer works correctly.
This was originally addressed in Mono BCL - see issue [11681](https://github.com/mono/mono/issues/11681) and has regressed in Blazor 5.0 update.
Affected package: [Blazor.LocalFiles](https://github.com/jburman/W8lessLabs.Blazor.LocalFiles)
[Example site](https://jburman.github.io/BlazorLocalFilesExample/) that uses package.

### To Reproduce
Create a blob URL with createObjectURL call in browser and attempt to access it via httpClient in Blazor.

### Exceptions (if any)
Receive error: Only 'http' and 'https' schemes are allowed. (Parameter 'requestUri')

### Further technical details
- ASP.NET Core version: 5.0.0-preview.8.20414.8

.NET SDK (reflecting any global.json):
 Version:   5.0.100-preview.8.20417.9
 Commit:    fc62663a35

Runtime Environment:
 OS Name:     Windows
 OS Version:  10.0.19041
 OS Platform: Windows
 RID:         win10-x64
 Base Path:   C:\Program Files\dotnet\sdk\5.0.100-preview.8.20417.9\

Host (useful for support):
  Version: 5.0.0-preview.8.20407.11
  Commit:  bf456654f9

- IDE: VS 16.8.0 Preview 2.0

review_comments: Do we need these if `typedArrayToURL` is returning a fixed url?
None of this is actually needed at all and it could just pass `blob:https://mdn.mozillademos.org/ca45b575-6348-4d3e-908a-3dbf3d146ea7` directly.

Is this url always expected to be around? Also, if it is meant as a fixed url, then we should move this to a static field, and use that in the tests, so that if it needs to change then all the uses are updated.

When creating a url like this `URL.createObjectURL` it will always be different so the url will never be fixed.  Just so happens to be fixed here because I took the test from  https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/Blob and the URL.createObjectURL does not exist in the JS engine.
I completely missed the comment right above that line. Maybe add a comment to explain your rationale, for people like me!
`HttpUtilities.IsHttpUri(requestUri)` - we return true now if `scheme==blob`. What happens if we have a url like `blob:not-http://foo/bar`? Should `false` be returned in that case?

No as this is created from the javascript environment normally with URL.createURLObject.  The browser environment in this case will handle the error if something went wrong.
